Excalibur. The legendary magical sword of King Arthur, granted to him by the mysterious Lady of the Lake and symbolic of Arthur's right to rule. The sword's origins, powers, and ultimate fate are central to Arthurian legend, representing not merely a weapon but a sign of divine favor and legitimate kingship.

Excalibur is sometimes conflated with the Sword in the Stone, the blade that establishes Arthur's birthright as king, but in most versions they are distinct swords, with Excalibur being the greater prize granted later by supernatural means. The Lady of the Lake, a mysterious magical being dwelling in an enchanted lake, presents Excalibur to Arthur alongside a magical scabbard that prevents wounds. The scabbard is said to be worth more than the sword itself because it grants invulnerability. The sword is described as having no equal in sharpness, durability, and magical properties. No armor can withstand its blade, and it never becomes dull or breaks, making it an instrument of divine will. Arthur wears Excalibur in all his great battles against the Saxons and in defense of Britain. The sword becomes so associated with his authority that losing it would mean losing his power to rule. In Malory's telling and other Arthurian romances, when Arthur falls mortally wounded at the Battle of Camlann, he commands Bedivere, his last remaining knight, to throw Excalibur back into the lake from which it came. Bedivere twice fails to obey, pocketing the sword because it seems too precious to surrender. Only on the third attempt does he finally hurl it into the water, where the Lady's hand emerges to catch it and withdraw it beneath the waves. Excalibur's return to the lake is interpreted as the sword's restoration to its divine source and a symbol of Arthur's passing from the mortal realm. The act is both an ending and a restoration of cosmic order, marking the end of the Arthurian age.
